# I/O ledger

Every way into and out of the target system's three MCUs -- each wire, sensor, switch, output, bus, supply and clock of the ECU board (two of them) and the Cockpit Controller -- with how the emulator models it physically, the faults it can inject, the knob that drives it and the test that exercises it. The source of truth is [`model/io_ledger.json`](../model/io_ledger.json); this page is generated from it.

`make io-coverage` runs the firmware you supply over a scripted run set (cold boot, engine start / run / stop with every switch moved, every menu, SD map load and datalog, firmware-update entry, both SD slots, every fault knob) with the emulator's I/O coverage recorder on, and fails if the firmware touched an SFR module, pin or ADC channel that is not in the ledger, or if an entry marked modelled has no test. The harness model behind every knob is `emu/common/s32board.c`; `s32pair --knobs` lists the knobs and the browser bench reaches the same ones through `s32_wasm_knob(name, value)`.

**Evidence:** DATASHEET (Microchip data sheet / device pack), DOCUMENTED (installation manual, drawings, operating procedures), OBSERVED (seen on the emulated system), MEASURED (on hardware), INFERRED (reasoned, not observed). **Modelled:** yes / partial / no. Package pins are the 100-pin TQFP numbering from the device packs (`model/mcu_io.json`).

| Flash controller (firmware-update flag page)<br>`ct.chip.nvm` | controller | NVM | NVMKEY unlock, page erase, row / word program | `emu/controller/tests/test_s32ct.c`<br>`emu/pair/test/io_faults.sh::ct_firmware_update_entry` | DATASHEET |
| Reset control<br>`ct.chip.reset` | controller | RESET | POR / MCLR through the harness; the core's own resets take the same path: RESET instruction (RCON.SWR), illegal opcode or illegal address mode (RCON.IOPUWR), hard-trap conflict (RCON.TRAPR). RCON keeps its flags across non-POR resets. BREAK with no debugger attached is treated as an illegal opcode (INFERRED-high: BREAK is not in the user instruction set). The uninitialized-W cause of IOPUWR is not detected. PIC24_ILLEGAL_STOPS=1 makes an illegal opcode stop the emulator instead (debug only) | `emu/pair/test/test_board.c::mclr_reset_events`<br>`emu/pic24/tests/test_core.c::illegal_opcode_resets`<br>`emu/pic24/tests/test_core.c::break_instruction`<br>`emu/controller/tests/test_s32ct.c::reset_causes_set_rcon_and_reset_peripherals`<br>`emu/pair/test/io_faults.sh::ct_firmware_update_resets` | DATASHEET |

## Limits: what is modelled only in part

* **ADC reference VREF+ / VREF-** (`ecu.an.vref`, partial): Reference drift / failure is not modelled separately (it is equivalent to scaling every channel).
* **LCD backlight PWM** (`ct.backlight`, partial): The OC1 output waveform itself is not generated (duty is read from the compare registers); dimming follows the ambient sensor.
* **LCD panel: RGB interface and panel-controller setup bus** (`ct.lcd`, partial): Panel-controller register contents are not decoded; panel faults (dead pixels, no backlight) are not modelled.

## Fault vocabulary

* `open`: wire or sensor open circuit
* `short_gnd`: short to ground
* `short_supply`: short to the supply / full scale
* `noise`: random noise on the signal
* `stuck`: value frozen
* `intermittent`: connection making and breaking
* `out_of_range`: a value outside the sensor's range
* `garbage`: protocol garbage / corrupted bytes on a bus
* `missing_edges`: edges not delivered
* `extra_edges`: spurious edges
* `timing`: edge timing or clock error
* `absent`: device not answering
* `power_loss`: supply removed
* `brownout`: supply sagging below the regulator's drop-out
